text:
anya: quick q — thinking about adding a lightweight perf smoke into the model onboarding pipeline to catch regressions earlier. tradeoff is cost vs coverage. idea: run 3 tiny microbenches (seq=32,256,1024) + a small golden prompt set and an ABI fingerprint. thoughts? :eyes:
chris: sgtm in principle. cost is the kicker. i'd do 100% for 32/256 fast checks, then sample 1-5% for the full 1024 bench depending on model size. also add a 'fast-fail' flag for obvious binary incompatibilities.
tejas: agree on sampling. one more signal we need: KV-cache warmup behavior. if we only run cold-prefix runs we'll miss steady-state perf regressions. recommend a short warmup stage (3 repetitions) for the 256/1024 cases.
marco: separate concerns: (1) binary/format compatibility (onnx/torchscript/quant) -> quick admit check, (2) perf smoke -> sampling + warmup, (3) quality evals -> separate stage. also propose canonical output for smoke: PASS / FLAKY / FAIL + tags (latency/correctness/abi).
anya: agreeing. quick config sketch i can add to onboarding YAML:```
smoke_runner:
  enabled: true
  quick_checks:
    - seq: 32
      repeats: 1
    - seq: 256
      repeats: 3
  heavy_checks:
    - seq: 1024
      repeats: 5
  sample_rate_heavy: 0.02
  thresholds:
    latency_p50_multiplier: 1.20
    failure_percentile: 95
  actions:
    on_fail: notify
    on_critical_fail: block_rollout
```
infra-bot: smoke-runner job queued: smoke-runner/1839991234 on aws-dedicated-3 · status=queued
chris: can infra attach a cost estimate to each run? want to expose "estimated GPU-minutes" in the UI so product can tune quotas.
ops-bot: noted — we'll add cost metadata to job events (label: est_gpu_minutes).
tejas: also: include a lightweight FLOP/param heuristic to decide heavy-sample probability. larger models -> lower sample_rate but higher priority for warmup. simple formula works: score = params^(0.5) / compute_factor.
anya: ok i'll add a draft RFC PR with the YAML and sampling heuristics. question: for on_critical_fail we said block_rollout — ops concerns? @marco? :shipit: 
marco: ops +1 for blocking on clear ABI/correctness FAIL. for perf regressions prefer halting canary and alerting rather than full rollback. default behavior: halt canary + postmortem required to proceed.
anya: perfect. i'll change on_critical_fail -> halt_canary in the draft and add a toggle for auto-rollback for experimental teams. will link spreadsheet with thresholds (baseline + 20% p50 or 5% token throughput drop triggers fail): https://docs.internal/redwood/perf-smoke-thresholds :+1:
chris: :+1: also add a test-mode flag so we can run smoke without consuming quota for dev-preview.
anya: done — thanks all. i'll open PR and ping reviewers.
